narrative_summary: SPX closed 7,515.34, pulling back ~0.8% after tagging the 6/15 swing high (7,578) — the tag-and-stall pattern at resistance persists rather than resolving into a breakout. The bull skeleton remains mechanically intact (50d > rising 200d, +7.83% over the 200-day, price above the 20/50-day), but the Monte Carlo edge has collapsed back to near-even (53.6% up-first, failing all thresholds), ERP is pinned at a zero-cushion 0.37% ceiling after the 10-year rose to 4.61%, and breadth (McClellan near its lows, net new highs weak) and credit still refuse to confirm the multi-week recovery. Trim bias into strength — not chasing the stall at resistance — remains the justified posture.
